children.label: Overview
children: Seeing the patient before surgery to identify risks that may affect recovery
Visit done one day before surgery
Aim: lower anesthetic and surgical morbidity and mortality, patient in optimal condition
Steps: problem identification, risk assessment, preoperative preparation, plan of anesthetic technique
Technique options: GA, laryngeal mask, endotracheal tube, spinal, epidural, local

children.label: Purposes
children: Document the condition needing surgery
Define the patient's medical and surgical problems
Arrange investigations, consultation and treatment if not optimal
Develop the anesthetic technique and perioperative care plan
Inform and reassure the patient
Reduce cost, hospital stay and cancellations

children.label: History
children: Brief history of present illness, current medications, allergies and reaction type
Past medical and surgical history, past anesthetic history
Family history of anesthetic problems
Functional inquiry and NPO status
Special attention to CVS, respiratory and neuromuscular systems
Unstable symptoms: postpone elective surgery for optimization

children.label: Cardiovascular and respiratory points
children: MI within 6 months or unstable angina: poor surgical candidate
Ask about exercise tolerance, arrhythmia or pacemaker, hypertension
Valvular disease: consider risk of subacute bacterial endocarditis
Active cardiac conditions: postpone except life-saving emergencies
COPD: baseline CO2 is high (50-60), avoid aggressive hyperventilation
Asthma: airway manipulation and cold dry gases trigger attacks
Acute URTI: postpone elective surgery about 6 weeks
Sleep apnea: may need postoperative ventilatory support

children.label: Smoking cessation timeline
children: Advise stopping at least 8 weeks before surgery
12-24 h: CO and nicotine levels fall
48-72 h: COHb normalizes, airway function improves
1-2 weeks: less sputum
4-6 weeks: PFTs improve
6-8 weeks: immune function normalizes
8-12 weeks: lower overall postoperative morbidity

children.label: Other conditions
children: Epilepsy: optimize antiepileptic dosing, avoid enflurane
Spinal cord injury: respiratory failure, autonomic hyperreflexia, hyperkalemia
Myasthenia gravis and NMJ disorders: unpredictable response to NMBs
Muscular dystrophy: higher malignant hyperthermia risk and postoperative respiratory failure
Diabetes: delayed gastric emptying, silent MI, stop oral hypoglycemics and use insulin sliding scale
Goitre: airway compression and tracheal deviation, inhalational induction preferred
Hyperthyroid: thyroid storm risk; hypothyroid: myocardial depression
GERD: H2 blocker, citrate, cricoid pressure
Long-term steroids: stress-dose steroids to prevent Addisonian crisis

children.label: Medications and allergies
children: Take cardiac and pulmonary medications with sips of water up to the day of surgery
Ask about penicillin, latex and propofol (egg) allergy
Lecturer: egg allergy is to egg white while propofol contains yolk lecithin
Metformin: stop a few days before surgery
Beta blockers decrease cardiovascular mortality
Asthmatics: avoid histamine-releasing drugs (morphine, atracurium)

children.label: Malignant hyperthermia and scoline apnea
children: MH: familial, fatal, triggered by inhalational agents (except N2O) and succinylcholine
MH preparation: total IV anesthesia, vaporizer disconnected, room ventilated 6 h, first case of the day
Dantrolene: lecturer stressed it only eases symptoms (standard teaching: the specific MH treatment)
Scoline apnea: pseudocholinesterase deficiency, prolongs ventilation, less dangerous than MH
Prolonged apnea in family suggests pseudocholinesterase deficiency; unexplained death suggests MH

children.label: Fasting guidelines
children: 8 h: meat, fried or fatty meal
6 h: light meal, infant formula, non-human milk
4 h: breast milk
2 h: clear fluids
Emergency with short fast: signed high-risk consent, rapid sequence induction with suxamethonium

children.label: Four fatal things in anesthesia
children: Malignant hyperthermia
Anaphylaxis
Aspiration
Disconnection of the circuit

children.label: Airway assessment
children: TMJ mobility: one-finger groove at the tragus on mouth opening
Mouth opening: three fingers should fit
Thyromental distance: less than 7 cm suggests difficult intubation
Mallampati I-II easy, III-IV difficult
Also tracheal centralization, upper lip bite (Calder) test, cervical spine mobility, Wilson score
Down syndrome (large tongue) and micrognathia: difficult intubation
Cervical spine disease (e.g. RA): awake intubation without neck extension

children.label: Investigations
children: CBC for every patient, others guided by history and examination
ECG: age over 50, hypertension, IHD signs, arrhythmia, diabetes over 40
Chest X-ray: cardiac or respiratory disease, malignancy, thoracic surgery
U&E, LFT, blood sugar, coagulation screen, urinalysis by indication
PFTs for dyspnea, COPD or asthma; cervical spine X-ray if difficult intubation predicted
ABG if dyspneic or cyanosed at rest, FEV1 below 60%, or thoracic surgery

children.label: ASA physical status
children: I: healthy patient
II: mild systemic disease, no limitation (also smoker, pregnant, obese, over 80 y)
III: severe systemic disease with definite limitation (e.g. IHD, COPD, morbid obesity)
IV: severe disease that is a constant threat to life
V: moribund, unlikely to survive 24 h
VI: brain dead organ donor; E = emergency
ASA IV and V need a high-risk consent signed by the family

children.label: Cardiac risk indices
children: Goldman: S3 or raised JVP 11, MI within 6 months 10, non-sinus rhythm 7, over 5 PVCs/min 7
Goldman: age over 70 5, emergency 4, poor health 3, major thoracic/abdominal/aortic surgery 3, aortic stenosis 3
Over 25 points: life-saving procedures only
RCRI factors: IHD, CHF, cerebrovascular disease, insulin-treated DM, creatinine over 2.0, high-risk surgery
RCRI event rate: 0 factors 0.5%, 1 factor 1.3%, 2 factors 3.6%, 3 or more 9.1%

children.label: Hypertension
children: Mild (140-159/90-99): no need to delay surgery
Moderate (160-179/100-109): review treatment, monitor closely
Severe (over 180/109): postpone elective surgery

children.label: Premedication
children: Reduce anxiety and pain, promote amnesia, reduce secretions
Reduce gastric volume and pH to avoid Mendelson's syndrome (aspiration pneumonitis)
Reduce PONV and vagal reflexes, enhance hypnosis, prevent endocarditis
H2 blocker or PPI hours before, oral sodium citrate 15-30 min before induction

children.label: High-risk groups
children: Elderly: fragile CVS, small doses cause hypotension, hypothermia risk
Emergency surgery in the elderly: 4 to 20 times higher mortality
Paediatrics: high risk, hypothermia risk
